description.p: Cordial loads Roblox's official Android x86-64 engine directly on Linux through a purpose-built runtime: the AOSP bionic linker, a bionic/glibc shim, a JNI VM in place of Android's, and a framework layer that answers the client's calls. No emulator, no container, no virtual machine.

Plugins are ordinary programs in their own processes, and they are granted named capabilities rather than access. There is no script execution, no hooking and no memory access — those are absent from the API rather than disabled, so there is no primitive to re-enable in a fork.
Cordial ships no Roblox code, APK or assets. You supply the Android client yourself.

It is early. Signing in, loading an experience and playing it with keyboard and mouse all work, text fields draw what you type, and sound plays. Voice chat does not, and on roughly one launch in three a signed-in client reaches the home screen and freezes; reopening usually works. Install it expecting rough edges.

Plugins can run. No package Cordial ships installed or bundled Deno, which plugins are written in, so they could not start on any install that did not already have one. Settings now offers to fetch a pinned interpreter where none is present, and the Arch package depends on it properly.

The AppImage can open a web view again; it bundled WebKit without the helper processes WebKit looks for by absolute path. Fixes a flash of the window background when chat opens, and a plugin consent prompt that asked again every time Settings was opened. The FastFlags editor is syntax-coloured and reports errors as you type, and Discord presence shows a game's own art with a default for games that send none.

Built-in plugins are started. They never were: Cordial looked in the user plugin directory and not the system one, so every plugin it ships was listed, granted and switched on without its process ever being spawned. Discord Rich Presence works as a result, recovers if Discord opens later, carries a game's own presence through BloxstrapRPC, and shows a join button.

Controllers are on by default, with a switch and a fix for a virtual mouse being reported as a pad. New settings for frame pacing, FastFlags and quitting when you leave a game. Plugins can be loaded unpacked from a folder and reload as they are edited.

The Flatpak works. Six separate faults stood between the packaged build and a running client, and every one was invisible from a source build: a linker compiled with PATH_MAX=256 that aborted at load, no access to the Roblox build the setup dialog pointed at, the session being written to disk instead of the keyring, every connection reading as metered, and no accessibility bus.

The application ID changes from org.cordial.Cordial to io.github.luohoa97.Cordial, which is an identifier this project controls. An existing install keeps its old data directory and will look freshly installed. The Flatpak also builds for the first time — it had been asking for a runtime with no GTK4 in it — and the published remote definition can now be added at all.

The app bridge is given the surface and platform parameters it was never handed, and everything Cordial fails to answer is collected into one report at exit. Graphics gains an explicit OpenGL ES option. Ctrl+V pastes into Roblox text boxes. Plugins run inside a kernel sandbox beneath Deno's permissions and the capability broker.

Sound comes out, and the microphone is open only while Roblox is recording. The pointer locks, and the launcher no longer imposes a session length. An earlier 1 fps report is withdrawn: it was the desktop, not the engine.

Keys work inside an experience: the engine wants evdev codes, not Android keycodes. Present mode MAILBOX gives a flat 60 where FIFO gave a variable 35 to 50. The engine cache now invalidates when the Roblox build changes, so a warm start runs the build you installed.

The first release anyone could use. Signing in works and the session persists in the desktop keyring rather than on disk; profiles isolate accounts so two run side by side; a native Wayland backend replaces the blank window; and the plugin brokers do something.
